review.description: Contributor comparison now explicitly separates independently owned mocked browser sessions from ordered shared-daemon scenarios, and retains repeated zero-retry timing samples without replacing full verification or release provenance. S4/S5 cover these fixture-only boundaries.
review.implementation: Reviewed playwright.config.ts project match/ignore partition, two-worker global cap and one-worker assembled cap. Browser benchmark checks exact PR source with read-only permissions, starts fresh servers per sample and stores separate JSON/time output. Existing performance configuration remains one worker with zero retries. Follow-up CI repair explicitly declares PyYAML 6.0.3 in hosted Python prerequisites and bounds each deterministic workflow-script subprocess with timeout=30; no browser scheduling, permissions or production behavior changes.
review.tests: test_browser_benchmark_retains_samples_and_stops_on_failure executes the workflow shell with deterministic subprocesses: asserts 1,2,1,2 worker sequence, no retries, distinct retained outputs and immediate exit 19 with partial evidence on failure. Full 158-title inventory and byte-identical 129 test statement comparison preserve original assertions. Reinspected subprocess argv, mocked npx, both exit-code subtests, exact worker/retry argv, retained JSON counts/content and GNU-time output assertion. The 30-second timeout applies to the whole deterministic shell invocation; clean Python 3.12 virtualenv verification installs only declared requirements before running the complete test_ci.py suite.
